claim_verdicts.evidence: "Secrets are similar to ConfigMaps but are specifically intended to hold confidential data." "A Secret is an object that contains a small amount of sensitive data such as a password, a token, or a key." "The values for all keys in the `data` field have to be base64-encoded strings."

"add an environment variable for each Secret key that you want to use to the `env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef` field." Task page: "If a container already consumes a Secret in an environment variable, a Secret update will not be seen by the container unless it is restarted." kubectl explain pod.spec.containers.env.valueFrom.secretKeyRef (1.34.3): "Selects a key of a secret in the pod's namespace".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/.../concepts/configuration/secret.md (Using Secrets as environment variables); refs/.../tasks/inject-data-application/distribute-credentials-secure.md; kubectl explain on kind-donhang

claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: "The `auth` value there is base64 encoded; it is obscured but not secret." and the docs themselves decode with `kubectl get secret ... -o jsonpath='{.data.*}' | base64 -d`. Local run: printf 'ZG9uaGFuZy1kZXYtcGFzc3dvcmQ=' | base64 -d → donhang-dev-password, no key involved. Round 2: added contrast 'unlike encryption, which cannot be turned back without a secret key' is definitional and consistent.

"Kubernetes Secrets are, by default, stored unencrypted in the API server's underlying data store (etcd)." Steps listed: "Enable Encryption at Rest for Secrets" (a page under tasks/administer-cluster). encrypt-data.md: "If you are running the kube-apiserver without the `--encryption-provider-config` command line argument, you do not have encryption at rest enabled."

"The commands `kubectl get` and `kubectl describe` avoid showing the contents of a `Secret` by default." Example output: "password:    12 bytes". Captured output: "POSTGRES_PASSWORD:   20 bytes"; live read-only `kubectl describe secret api -n donhang` → "ConnectionStrings__Default:  71 bytes".

"Anyone with API access can retrieve or modify a Secret, and so can anyone with access to etcd. Additionally, anyone who is authorized to create a Pod in a namespace can use that access to read any Secret in that namespace". Round 2: section 4 now lists all three paths (claim 14), so the earlier overstatement is gone.

tools/extract-code deploy/k8s/api.yaml --tag stage-2 --lines 25-38 is identical to the lesson block: envFrom.configMapRef.name: api; env ConnectionStrings__Default valueFrom.secretKeyRef name: api, key: ConnectionStrings__Default.

"Each object in your cluster has a Name that is unique for that type of resource." "you can have one Pod and one Deployment that are each named `myapp-1234`." Live read-only: `kubectl get configmap/api secret/api -n donhang` lists both.

git -C examples/don-hang grep "kind: Secret" stage-2 → no match. stage-2:scripts/k8s/secrets.sh: "set -a; . ./.env; set +a" under "# Read the values from .env without printing them.", then secret db/api/keycloak via `kubectl create secret generic "$name" -n donhang "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - -o name`.

create secret generic: "If client strategy, only print the object that would be sent, without sending it." apply: "This resource will be created if it doesn't exist yet." Run: `kubectl create secret generic rv-x -n donhang --from-literal=k=v --dry-run=client -o yaml` printed the Secret (data k: dg==); `kubectl get secret rv-x` → NotFound.

Lesson output block equals examples/don-hang/outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/secrets.txt line for line (Type: Opaque; POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 20 bytes; ZG9uaGFuZy1kZXYtcGFzc3dvcmQ=; donhang-dev-password). 'donhang-dev-password' is 20 bytes (wc -c).

Ran both Try-it commands on kind-donhang (read-only); compared in shell without printing: decoded Secret api == printenv in deployment/api == "Host=db;Database=donhang;Username=donhang;Password=donhang-dev-password".

secret.md caution: "Anyone with API access can retrieve or modify a Secret, and so can anyone with access to etcd. Additionally, anyone who is authorized to create a Pod in a namespace can use that access to read any Secret in that namespace; this includes indirect access such as the ability to create a Deployment." Lesson sentence now names all three paths.

secret.md: "If the Secret cannot be fetched (perhaps because it does not exist, or due to a temporary lack of connection to the API server) the kubelet periodically retries running that Pod." configmap.md (same mechanism for env): "the kubelet uses the data from the ConfigMap when it launches container(s) for a Pod." Task page: env Secret updates not seen "unless it is restarted".

rbac.md: rules name resources ("resources: [\"pods\", \"pods/log\"]"); also "You can also refer to resources by name ... through the `resourceNames` list", so read permission is not only per kind. Live, temporary objects: Role rv-cm-reader (get configmaps) bound to SA rv-sa → `auth can-i get configmap/api` yes, `get secret/api` no; objects deleted.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Permission to read can be granted per kind of object, so a cluster can let someone read the ConfigMap `api` but not the Secret `api`.

claim_verdicts.evidence: secret.md: "When you create a Secret using `kubectl`, you must use the `generic` subcommand to indicate an `Opaque` Secret type." generic ref: --from-literal "Specify a key and literal value to insert in secret (i.e. mykey=somevalue)". Task page decodes `-o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode`. Run: create secret generic rv-s --from-literal=K1=hello → .type Opaque, {.data.K1} aGVsbG8=; deleted.

issues.quote: Permission to read is granted per kind of object,
issues.text: Slightly too absolute: RBAC grants per resource kind but can also narrow to single objects (rbac.md: "refer to resources by name ... through the `resourceNames` list"). The consequence in the sentence is correct (verified live with a temporary Role).
issues.fix: Replace 'Permission to read is granted per kind of object' with 'Permission to read can be granted per kind of object'. No other change.
